Slop Resize · free, in your browser

Resize many images at once

Drop dozens or hundreds of photos and give them all the same size: a width, a height, a long edge or a percentage. Slop Resize does them one by one on your device and hands you a ZIP.

Resize images in bulk

How to do it

  1. Drop your photos on the page, or choose Open…. Each one joins the queue.
  2. Under Resize by, pick Width and height, Percentage or Long edge, and type the size. Long edge 1920 is set for you.
  3. Choose the Picture format (JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF where your browser can write it) and the quality.
  4. Press Resize all (Ctrl+Enter). Each row shows the size before and after.
  5. Choose Download all (zip) to get every result in one file.

Long edge is the easy choice for a mixed batch: portrait and landscape photos both end up with their longer side at the size you pick, and keep their shape. The originals are never changed; the results are copies named like photo-1920x1280.jpg.

Your files stay on this device: Slop Resize runs in your browser, with no upload, no account and no watermark.

Questions

How many images can I resize at once?

There is no fixed number. The queue works through the files one at a time on your device, so a big batch just takes longer.

Will the photos keep their proportions?

Yes, with Long edge or Percentage, and with Width and height when Keep aspect ratio is ticked. Untick it only if you want to stretch.

Are my photos uploaded?

No. Every picture is decoded, resized and encoded in your browser.

Can I save my settings for next time?

Yes. Save the settings as a preset; they are kept in Slop Drive, or in this browser without it.
